related_questions.question: Where is the safest place to be in an earthquake?

text_blocks.snippet: The safest place to be during an earthquake is under a sturdy table or desk, holding on to it (Drop, Cover, and Hold On). If no sturdy furniture is available, get next to an interior wall away from windows and cover your head and neck with your arms. If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, power lines, and other hazards.
snippet_highlighted_words: under a sturdy table or desk, holding on to it (Drop, Cover, and Hold On)

list.title: Drop, Cover, and Hold On:
list.snippet: Immediately drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy table or desk, and hold on to it. This protects you from falling debris.

list.title: If no sturdy furniture is available:
list.snippet: Get next to an interior wall, away from windows, and cover your head and neck with your arms.

list.title: Stay away from:
list.snippet: Windows, mirrors, tall furniture, and exterior walls as these are the most likely places for things to fall or break.

list.title: Do not:
list.snippet: Run outside or use elevators, as the shaking can make it dangerous to move around and elevators can fail.

list.title: If in bed:
list.snippet: Stay in bed and protect your head with a pillow.

list.title: Move to an open area:
list.snippet: Get away from buildings, power lines, trees, and other hazards that could fall.

list.title: Drop to the ground:
list.snippet: Stay low and cover your head and neck with your arms until the shaking stops.
Pull over: Safely pull over to a clear location away from buildings, power lines, and other hazards.
Stay inside: Do not exit the vehicle until the shaking stops.
Practice Drop, Cover, and Hold On: Regularly practice this drill so you can react quickly and safely during an earthquake.
Stay Informed: Follow official safety guidelines and instructions from local authorities.
Be aware of your surroundings: Identify potential hazards in your home or workplace and take steps to minimize risks.
Don't panic: Stay calm and focus on protecting yourself and others.
